messages.subject: INLA model that previously ran is now crashing
parts:
Hello, 

I am moving all of my code over to a new computing cluster (a Linux machine). I was able to run the model in question without problem yesterday, when I realized I had not set OMP_NUM_THREADS and INLA was not using all 8 threads I have access to. After setting OMP_NUM_THREADS=8, suddenly the model crashes. The output is below, any insights would be appreciated (a single thread is fine for this model, but I need more computing power later in my code, and for validating this model).

Many thanks,
Julianne

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA model that previously ran is now crashing
parts:
if you want to run many models, and have a cluster, I would consider
to run several models in parallel, each on with num.threads=1, which
would be more efficient (my preferred strategy).

the argument num.threads, is a suggestion of max number of threads.
the actual number of threads used depends on the number of
hyperparameters but also where in the code we are. there is a system
in place for trying to do this efficiently, like small models are
always run in serial mode and does not depend on num.threads.

using the PARDISO library, then there are more options, see
inla.pardiso() and therein.

H
